full_judgment:
Defendant-Petitioner Rezaul Karim obtained a higher degree in technical matter in Electronics from UK and took lease of shop No. 7 in a building known as "J and J Mansion" situated at 2, Dhanmondi Residential Area, Road No. 13, Dhaka on the basis of a written agreement dated 1.5.81 for a period of 20 years at the initial rent of Tk. 1,000.00 per month which is revisable after every five years and also paid a salami of Tk. 1,22,000.00 and the petitioner was put into the possession of the shop on that day. Petitioner started Electronics business under name and style M/s "(Arkay's Electronics)". Petitioner followed the terms and conditions of the lease deed in letter and spirit. At the time of execution of the said lease deed dated 1.5.81 plaintiff opposite party promised to register the lease deed at a convenient time. Defendant believed that promise and prayed for registration of the lease deed on several occasions. After expiry of 5 years terms of the deed of lease, the rent was revised and it was increased from Tk. 1,000.00 to 1,700.00 per month and the plaintiff opposite party executed the supplementary deed of lease on 1.5.86 which is marked as Annexure 'B' to the petition. 

 3. Trouble arose when RAJUK (the then DIT) gave notice to the said land lady and others to demolish shops and unauthorised construction and the petitioner as a tenant also got one notice to that effect. Subsequently RAJUK issued an order to stop demolition and gave 6 months time to the owner of the building to regularise the construction of the shop. Plaintiff opposite party did not take any step to regularise the unauthorised construction of the shop. Defendant-Petitioner gave Advocate notice to the plaintiff opposite party on 22.3.88 requesting her to regularise unauthorised construction of the shop and to stop the impending demolition. The copy of the letter marked as Annexure 'D' to the petition. 

 4. Plaintiff opposite party land lady with a malafide intention stopped accepting rent of the shop from the month of July, 1988 to prove the petitioner to be a defaulter. So the petitioner to avoid to be a defaulter started depositing rent, in, the Rent Controller's Court, Dhaka vide HR case No. 34 of 1988. 

 11. In reply to this contention the learned advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that the learned Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka committed no illegality in passing the impugned order and as such it cannot be interfered with in revisional jurisdiction. It is further submitted that different issues are involved in two different suits and in the earlier suit eviction of the defendant petitioner has been sought and in the subsequent suit a verbal contract is sought to be enforced and in view of the fact the relief sought for in both the suits are not identical. It is further submitted by the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party that the earlier suit cannot be stayed till disposal of the subsequent suit and in support of his contention he relied on section 10 CPC. 

 13. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that he does not want the earlier Title Suit No. 365 of 1988 (for eviction) to be stayed till disposal of the subsequent suit (TS No. 62 of 1990). His simple submission is that both the suits be tried analogously since the parties, subject matter, cause of actions in both the suits are identical and for that purpose an application under section 151 CPC was filed for consolidation of both the suits. It is further submitted that in a consolidated suit the issues are not necessarily to be identical and cogent. In fact, this submission appears to be well founded. Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not go to the root of the jurisdiction of the Court trying the second suit but merely lays down a rule of procedure. The words "no Court shall proceed with the trial of any suit" are intended to bar the separate trial of any suit in which the matter in issues was also directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit between the same parties in the same court. But these words do not apply to the simultaneous hearing latter and earlier suits after consolidation of hearing of the suits. The matter in issue involved in both suits referred above are directly and substantially the same. Section 10 CPC does not intend to take away inherent power of the Court to consolidate in the interest of justice in appropriate cases. In the previously instituted suit (TS No. 365 of 1988) defendant-petitioner who was inducted as tenant in shop No. 7 is sought to be evicted there from. But in the subsequent suit (TS No. 62 of 1990) a verbal contract is sought to be enforced in respect of the same subject matter i.e. a shop, No. 7. In this connection a lease deed vide Annexure 'A' has been filed which purports to show lease was in respect of shop No. 7 for a period of 20 years and that plaintiff opposite party it is alleged, promised that in due course a registered deed of lease to be executed by her and since despite demands no deed of lease was registered as promised. So subsequent suit being TS No. 62 of 1990 was instituted for specific performance of contract. 

 15. It is settled law that the very nature of the principle of consolidation implies that similarity of identity of the matter in issue in different suits by the same party should be decided by the court once and for all. The object of consolidation is to avoid multiplicity of litigations between the same parties whenever the matter in issue is substantially or directly the same. High Court in appropriate cases should interfere with the order of subordinate Court refusing to consolidate, as the principle of consolidation in no way conflicts with the purpose of section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure; on the contrary it preserves and promotes it. Certain meaning of Statute must not impute to the legislature to create situation leading to an absurd result and offending against common sense. On the contrary it is the duty of the judiciary to give as far as possible an interpretation of law which inspires confidence in all reasonable manner. 

 17. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party lastly submits that he has no objection to both the suits being tried analogously if such trial is held within three months from receipt of this Court's order by the trial Court. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party apprehends that subsequent suit (TS No. 62 of 1990) wherein Government has been impleaded as party may take innumerable adjournments for filing the written statement and thereby the disposal of both suits is likely to be delayed and so the learned Advocate contends that a definite date should be fixed within which Government be directed to file written statement, else Government be debarred from filing written statement. This apprehension of the learned Advocate for the opposite party cannot be said to be without unfoundation. Government in fact is not a necessary party but a formal party to be impleaded in this suit in compliance with the provision of PO No. 142 of 1972. Further it appears from the certified copy of the plaint of TS No. 62 of 1990 (vide Annexure 'E') to the petition, Government has been impleaded as proforma defendant. However, if Government does not file written statement within the period of three months from the date of receipt of this order by the trial court, the Government will be debarred from filing written statement. The Government Advocate be informed accordingly.
